title: JavaScript Map and Set collections
concepts: Choosing maps, sets, and objects by access pattern

inventory.title: Map constructor, properties, methods, and symbols
Set constructor, properties, methods, and symbols

accuracyFacts: Map and Set key/value equality uses SameValueZero semantics: NaN equals NaN for membership, positive and negative zero identify one entry, and objects compare by identity. The stored key for negative zero is canonicalized to positive zero. Updating an existing Map key does not move its insertion position; deleting and re-adding it appends it at the end.

Map iterators and Map.prototype.forEach observe mutations while iteration is active: entries deleted before being reached are skipped; appended entries may be visited; deleting and re-adding an already visited key can cause it to be visited again. Iteration is not a snapshot.

Map.groupBy consumes an iterable, calls the callback once per item with (value, zero-based index), and uses each callback result directly as a Map key. It returns a new Map whose values are arrays containing original element references in encounter order. It does not coerce keys to property strings.

Map.prototype.getOrInsert returns a present value even when that value is undefined; otherwise it stores and returns the supplied value. getOrInsertComputed validates a callable callback, skips it when the key exists, otherwise calls it with key and undefined this-argument, then rechecks and overwrites a same-key reentrant entry with the computed result. Eager default expressions are evaluated before getOrInsert is called.

Set composition and relation methods accept a set-like object, not merely an iterable. The required protocol reads size, has, and keys; keys must be callable and return an iterable when an algorithm iterates it. A plain iterable without these members is insufficient. Native Map is set-like because its keys() returns keys and its size/has match that protocol.

Set.prototype.union keeps this Set's insertion order and appends previously absent values in the other object's keys iteration order. difference preserves this Set's order. symmetricDifference emits values unique to this Set in this order, followed by values unique to the other keys iteration. intersection's output order depends on relative sizes: it iterates this Set when this size is no larger, otherwise iterates other.keys().

The seven Set composition/relationship methods were standardized in ECMAScript 2025. They produce ordinary Set results and do not use Set[Symbol.species]. Map[Symbol.species] and Set[Symbol.species] remain standardized accessor properties returning the receiver constructor, but MDN documents both accessors as unused by their respective current Map/Set methods.

Map.prototype.getOrInsert and Map.prototype.getOrInsertComputed were standardized in ECMAScript 2026 and are marked Baseline 2026 by MDN; older browsers and runtimes may lack them. Map.groupBy was standardized in ECMAScript 2024 and has broad browser availability since March 2024 per MDN. Earlier implementations used the transitional Array.prototype.groupToMap name; current standard code uses Map.groupBy.

The Map and Set specifications require average access times sublinear in collection size, but do not require a particular backing structure or promise constant-time operations. The specification's list-based algorithms describe observable behavior, not required implementation details.

Set-like size is read and converted with ToNumber and ToIntegerOrInfinity; NaN and negative results throw, non-integers are truncated, and positive Infinity is permitted. The protocol then requires callable has and keys properties.

Map.prototype and Set.prototype are non-writable, non-enumerable, non-configurable constructor properties. Their shared prototype objects are ordinary objects without [[MapData]]/[[SetData]], so inherited size getters and collection methods throw TypeError when invoked with those prototypes as receivers.

Map.groupBy is the current ES2024 static API; older browser implementations used the transitional Array.prototype.groupToMap name. Object own-key enumeration has distinct ordering rules: array-index string keys in numeric order, other strings in creation order, then symbols in creation order.
